# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260927-0708-858-partners-validation`
- Research system: `Codex web research`
- Started at: `2026-09-27 07:08 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-27 07:15 CDT`
- Research scope: First-party client, partner, event, and market-positioning page validation for 858 Partners
- Queue item or vendor: `competitor:858-partners`
- Methodology: Candidate-page validation and first-party competitor/client research

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 4 relationship groups covering 34 named client-event appearances across 25 unique technology providers
- Company/competitor profile observations added or revised: 3
- Conflicts found: 3
- Material takeaway: 858 Partners is not supported as a core restaurant software vendor. Its first-party pages position it as a restaurant-technology advisory, investment, commercial-guidance, and executive-community layer that brings technology clients into curated operator forums. Four 2026 event recaps directly name technology providers as 858 clients or partners, including Olo, Toast, Restaurant365, Bikky, Bite, Crunchtime, Deepgram, Loop, Momos, With Coverage, and others. These pages establish advisory/event relationships, not restaurant deployments or proof that attendee brands use the participating vendors.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: Bikky; Toast; Deepgram; PreciTaste; Momos; Olo; Restaurant365; With Coverage
- Vendor: 858 Partners
- Product or category: Restaurant-technology commercial guidance, client representation, curated operator access, and event activation
- Relationship indication: partner
- Deployment scope: unknown
- Evidence type: partner page
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: 858's first-party Dallas recap explicitly says eight 858 client companies anchored the event and names representatives from eight unique technology providers.
- Source title: Dallas NEST Chapter Gathering 2026 Event Recap
- Source URL: https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/dallas-2026
- Publisher or source owner: 858 Partners
- Published date, if known: 2026
- Accessed date: 2026-09-27
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The page says eight 858 client companies anchored the March 26 gathering at CEC Entertainment headquarters and later names Bikky, Toast, Deepgram, PreciTaste, Momos, Olo, Restaurant365, and With Coverage representatives.
- Product-specific evidence: The relationship is described as client participation in an 858/NEST event designed to connect restaurant operators with technology partners by priority area.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page does not disclose engagement terms, investment status, duration, or whether every named representative's employer was a current advisory client beyond the event. Participation does not prove deployment by attending restaurant brands.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current engagement status and service scope through an 858 portfolio/client page or provider announcement.

### Observation 2

- Brand: Bite; Loop; Revenue Management Solutions; Toast; Deepgram; Momos; Rokt; Restaurant365; Olo; With Coverage
- Vendor: 858 Partners
- Product or category: Restaurant-technology commercial guidance, client representation, executive access, and conference activation
- Relationship indication: partner
- Deployment scope: unknown
- Evidence type: partner page
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: 858's first-party RLC recap says its three activations were run in partnership with ten clients and names representatives from these ten unique technology providers in the client/partner section.
- Source title: RLC 2026
- Source URL: https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/rlc-2026
- Publisher or source owner: 858 Partners
- Published date, if known: 2026
- Accessed date: 2026-09-27
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The page says 858 hosted three Restaurant Leadership Conference activations in partnership with ten clients, welcomed more than 250 brand executives, and used 858 House as a private meeting venue for client executives and operators.
- Product-specific evidence: The page describes curated workshops, executive meetings, a private hospitality lounge, and a C-suite luncheon rather than a software product.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The attendee roster repeats companies and does not label each row individually as a client. It establishes event participation and collective client support but does not disclose contract or investment details. Operator attendance is not proof of vendor adoption.
- Recommended follow-up: Cross-check current client status on the named providers' announcements and distinguish advisory clients from event sponsors.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Checkmate; Loop; Momos; Olo; Qu; RevMo; unPLUG
- Vendor: 858 Partners
- Product or category: Off-premise executive forum, client representation, and operator-to-technology-provider access
- Relationship indication: partner
- Deployment scope: unknown
- Evidence type: partner page
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: 858's first-party Food on Demand recap thanks its clients and partners and names representatives from seven unique technology providers immediately below that section.
- Source title: 2026 Food on Demand Executive Leadership Luncheon
- Source URL: https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/food-on-demand-2026
- Publisher or source owner: 858 Partners
- Published date, if known: 2026
- Accessed date: 2026-09-27
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The page describes a 100-operator luncheon representing 41,500 locations, thanks clients and partners for seeding operator conversations, and lists Checkmate, Loop, Momos, Olo, Qu, RevMo, and unPLUG representatives.
- Product-specific evidence: 858 provided intentional seating, a guided workshop, pre-event networking, and facilitated peer discussion around first-party growth and third-party marketplace economics.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page groups clients and partners together, so the exact commercial relationship type for each named company is not disclosed. It does not support any restaurant-brand deployment claim.
- Recommended follow-up: Separate advisory clients, event sponsors, and ecosystem partners using provider-side disclosures.

### Observation 4

- Brand: Bikky; Bite; Crunchtime; Deepgram; Momos; Olo; PayPal; Toast; With Coverage; Ziosk
- Vendor: 858 Partners
- Product or category: Restaurant-technology advisory/community participation and operator workshop activation
- Relationship indication: partner
- Deployment scope: unknown
- Evidence type: partner page
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: 858's first-party Chicago recap says ten 858 client companies were represented and names representatives from ten unique technology providers in its gratitude/client section.
- Source title: 2026 Chicago NEST Chapter Gathering
- Source URL: https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/all-nest-2026
- Publisher or source owner: 858 Partners
- Published date, if known: 2026
- Accessed date: 2026-09-27
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The page says ten 858 client companies joined more than 100 attendees, including nearly 70 restaurant-brand executives, and identifies Bikky, Bite, Crunchtime, Deepgram, Momos, Olo, PayPal, Toast, With Coverage, and Ziosk representatives.
- Product-specific evidence: 858 developed a one-hour guest-data workshop and structured small peer groups pairing restaurant operators with technology partners.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page does not disclose whether all relationships are advisory, investment, sponsorship, or event-only engagements. Named attendance does not prove product adoption by any operator in the room.
- Recommended follow-up: Verify present-day client status and relationship type from provider-side sources.

## Company / competitor profile observations

### Competitor profile observation 1

- Target: `competitor:858-partners`
- Field: synopsis
- Value or observation: 858 Partners operates as a restaurant-technology advisory, investment, commercial-guidance, and executive-community firm. Its public operating model centers on curating restaurant operator forums, representing technology clients, developing workshops, and facilitating commercial access rather than selling a restaurant operating system.
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Four detailed first-party 2026 recaps consistently describe the same model across multiple events and client cohorts.
- Source title: Dallas, RLC, Food on Demand, and Chicago 2026 event recaps
- Source URL: https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/dallas-2026
- Publisher or source owner: 858 Partners
- Published date, if known: 2026
- Accessed date: 2026-09-27
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The pages repeatedly describe 858 clients, curated operator conversations, technology-partner participation, intentional seating, workshops, executive meetings, and conference activations.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The pages are self-authored marketing recaps and do not disclose revenue mix, formal portfolio structure, or the boundary between advisory clients, investments, sponsors, and partners.

### Competitor profile observation 2

- Target: `competitor:858-partners`
- Field: strengths
- Value or observation: Demonstrated convening access across restaurant C-suite, technology, digital, operations, finance, and off-premise leaders, with repeatable formats that place technology clients into curated small-group discussions and meetings with restaurant operators.
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: The four pages report events ranging from roughly 50 to more than 250 brand executives and consistently describe structured operator-client interaction.
- Source title: 858 Partners 2026 event recaps
- Source URL: https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/rlc-2026
- Publisher or source owner: 858 Partners
- Published date, if known: 2026
- Accessed date: 2026-09-27
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The RLC recap describes more than 250 brand executives and client meeting activity; Dallas describes more than 50 brand executives; Food on Demand describes 100 operators representing 41,500 locations; Chicago describes nearly 70 restaurant-brand executives.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: Attendance and satisfaction figures are reported by 858 and are not independently audited. They demonstrate reach, not conversion or product adoption.

### Competitor profile observation 3

- Target: `competitor:858-partners`
- Field: key_customers
- Value or observation: Named 2026 client or client/partner relationships include Bikky, Bite, Checkmate, Crunchtime, Deepgram, Loop, Momos, Olo, PayPal, PreciTaste, Qu, Restaurant365, Revenue Management Solutions, RevMo, Rokt, Toast, unPLUG, With Coverage, and Ziosk; the exact relationship type and current status varies or is not disclosed.
- Confidence: 85%
- Confidence rationale: Each name appears in a first-party 858 recap under language describing clients, clients and partners, or client companies represented; confidence is reduced because engagement terms and duration are not public.
- Source title: 858 Partners 2026 event recaps
- Source URL: https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/all-nest-2026
- Publisher or source owner: 858 Partners
- Published date, if known: 2026
- Accessed date: 2026-09-27
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Dallas explicitly says eight client companies; RLC says ten clients; Chicago says ten client companies; Food on Demand thanks clients and partners before listing representatives.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: A named event appearance may reflect advisory work, investment, sponsorship, partnership, or event participation. This observation should not be converted into a canonical customer list without relationship-type review.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: 858 Partners is a core POS, payments, ordering, loyalty, or restaurant-operations software vendor.
- Pages checked: All four validated 2026 event recaps.
- Result: Not supported. The pages describe advisory, commercial-guidance, investment/community, event, workshop, and operator-access functions.

- Candidate or claim: Restaurant brands attending 858 events are customers of the technology providers named on the same pages.
- Pages checked: All four validated 2026 event recaps.
- Result: Not supported. The pages establish co-presence and curated discussions, not adoption or deployment.

- Candidate or claim: Every named technology provider has the same current commercial relationship with 858.
- Pages checked: All four validated 2026 event recaps.
- Result: Not supported. Language varies among clients, client companies, clients and partners, and event participation; no contract terms or current-status dates are disclosed.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/dallas-2026 | partner page | 2026-09-27 | Observation 1; profile observations | Productive first-party page; explicitly says eight 858 client companies. |
| https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/rlc-2026 | partner page | 2026-09-27 | Observation 2; profile observations | Productive first-party page; describes ten client partnerships and 858 House meetings. |
| https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/food-on-demand-2026 | partner page | 2026-09-27 | Observation 3; profile observations | Productive first-party page; groups clients and partners, so individual relationship type remains uncertain. |
| https://www.858partners.com/post-event-recap/all-nest-2026 | partner page | 2026-09-27 | Observation 4; profile observations | Productive first-party page; explicitly says ten 858 client companies were represented. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: 858 Partners competes with Genius indirectly through influence over vendor selection, commercial access, and restaurant-technology ecosystem positioning, not through a directly substitutable POS or commerce product.
- Inference: 858's repeated relationships with Olo, Toast, Restaurant365, Bite, Bikky, Deepgram, Momos, and With Coverage suggest a broad, multi-category client network; repetition across events is stronger evidence of an ongoing relationship than a single appearance, but still does not disclose contract status.
- Review-first constraint: These observations belong in the intelligence-drop intake path. Do not promote event co-presence into canonical restaurant deployments, or classify every named provider as a current customer, without morning-cycle review.
